Distribution and habitat ecology. Currently, Paramesotriton wumengshanensis sp. nov. is found only in three deep-water pools in the type locality. This area has a mean annual temperature of approximately 20 ° C and receives about 1,800 mm of annual precipitation, with a humid subtropical monsoon climate. Surrounding the waterholes are bamboo forests and local crops, including rice, corn, and chili peppers. During a survey in July 2018, several other species were also recorded at the type locality, including Triplophysa wulongensis Chen, Sheraliev, Shu & Peng, 2021; Rhinogobius giurinus Rutter, 1897; Tylototriton kweichowensis Fang & Chang, 1932; Boulenophrys qianbeiensis (Su, Shi, Wu, Li, Yao, Wang & Li, 2020); Oreolalax rhodostigmatus Hu & Fei, 1979 (tadpoles); Hyla annectans (Jerdon, 1870); and Odorrana grahami (Boulenger, 1917). The primary threat to the species comes from ongoing mineral development in the upper reaches of the rivers within its range, which has caused the water in the mainstem rivers to become discolored (blackened), thus restricting the species to deep pools on the riverbanks. Currently, there have been no reports of illegal human capture. However, more ecological and reproductive information on this species is still lacking.
